product_from_film: ChatGPT Voice is presented as a phone conversation partner for everyday questions, fact checking and translation.
explains_well: People ask questions while repeated phone close-ups link their reactions to the same simple voice screen.
unclear: The sampled images and error-prone transcript cannot verify natural turn taking, latency, answer accuracy or translation quality.

categories.finding: Silent pictures show phone conversation and reactions, but reasoning and translation benefits need speech or captions.
Phone close-ups isolate one orb and a few controls, while faces carry the surrounding scene.
The fact-check section lasts roughly 57s with similar framing; its information depends heavily on the spoken exchange.
Opening everyday use is followed by more everyday requests and a shared social example.
Smiles, reaction close-ups and a shared table may make the tool feel approachable; audience response was not measured.
One room, repeated orb UI and repeated yellow title tie all presenters together.
The film presents examples and claims through conversation. Stills and ASR cannot verify full-duplex behavior, factual answers or live translation.
Yellow script title and recurring domestic set distinguish the presentation from a dashboard demo.
A short visible question-and-answer caption in the long fact-check section could clarify its purpose when muted.

lessons.keep: Return to the same clear phone screen between human reactions so the device remains connected to the story.
try: Add two short question-and-answer captions to the fact-check exchange and compare muted comprehension.
For Tin, film one user making a visible correction to a generated post, then show the saved result in the same setting.
lessons.avoid: Using smiling reactions as evidence of factual accuracy or low latency.
lessons.open: Voice quality, overlap handling, transcript accuracy, translation accuracy and edited versus real response timing remain unknown.
